In rollout 1, PF1 was revealed by A2 at turn 0 ("a private, prearranged five-minute regulation break in the library — it prevents the escalation entirely") and was properly cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's decisions include regulation_break_location="library" and regulation_break_minutes=5, both correct. The failing field is correction_response, which the settlement set to "Replace public verbal corrections with private redirection; prearranged proactive regulation break triggered before escalation". The check C6 apparently requires the correction_response to encode the specific response sequence that PF1's why statement calls out: "private correction followed by exactly a five-minute library regulation break." The settlement's wording leads with private redirection and mentions a proactive break, but it does not state the break as a sequential follow-up to the private correction, and it adds "triggered before escalation" language that is not part of PF1's stated implication. The passing rollouts (0, 2, 3) used phrasings like "Avoid public verbal corrections; use private redirection strategies" (rollout 0) and "Replace public verbal corrections with private redirection; offer prearranged regulation breaks before antecedent triggers arise" (rollout 2), so the check tolerates some variation, but rollout 1's specific wording fell outside the accepted encoding. This is a check-wording/encoding problem, not a disclosure or misapplied-information problem. (2) C8 (linked to PF3, owner A4): ENCODING MISMATCH. In rollout 1, PF3 was revealed by A4 at turn 1 ("all updates must be sent by text message in Spanish at the end of each school day") and was properly cited in justification_fact_ids. The settlement's decisions include family_update_language="Spanish" (correct) and family_update_method="text message at end of each school day". The passing rollouts used "daily end-of-day text message" (rollout 0) and "daily end-of-day text message" (rollout 2), both containing "daily." Rollout 1's omission of the word "daily" caused the mismatch despite the information being correctly revealed and cited.
